title: Buddy's Blue Melody Boys and Jack Teagarden's first Shreveport trio
summary: After Lake Charles in 1923 Kelly helps form the Blue Melody Boys, touring by Ford and booked by Jasper Tompkins; Teagarden first plays Shreveport with a trio.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: So, uh. Ham sent us to Lake Charles, which is where I heard some early little bands we used to play. Big Lake and we played Shaw Beach, Pleasure Field. At that time, it was a real nice resort out in the lake. That was before Lake Charles became the Dakota Port. And, we were swimming and then we had a ballroom out over the world. And, it was real nice. We're talking about 1923 now. And, um. So, after leaving Lake Charles, this group of fellas, Brooks Prud and Dick Coleman and Buddy Seabee and myself, went back to Shreveport and organized the Buddies Blue Melody Boys. Buddies Blue Melody Boys was the group that I was identified with for most of the several years that I first played. And, it was a very good band of the time. Some of the best musicians would, of course, would go through this band. We had the same personnel, but sometimes we played together as long as two years without single change. We all had all head arrangements. We, uh. We were really together and had a great time. Played all through North Texas, East Texas, New Cork, Mississippi, Arkansas. And, we did this in the Ford automobile. At first, with ice and glass curtains, we packed up, sometimes six guys, strap all of the stuff on the back of the Ford. And, we were booked. There was an interesting thing. We were booked by a man named Jasper Tompkins. We were booked, oh, dozens of names. Black names they had white names they had. And, first time Jack Teagarden played in Shreveport, he played for Jasper Tompkins. Played with Terry Sheehan and Reginald Gullick. They had a trio.

Gullick. And, Thomas Joyner. Now, these are names you may not be familiar with, but they're well-known, well-well-known at this time. But, Jack was the outstanding star. Is that the same as Tommy Joyner?
Is his name as Tallis? Yeah. What did you call him? Tommy?
Tommy, uh-huh. And, he played, that's the drummer on Zalifon.
Yeah, that's right. I've heard of him. He's from Tyler, Texas, too, sir.
Oh, I see. And, uh... And, the other man you mentioned before him, there's Terry Sheehan and somebody in between.
I didn't get what he played. Well, actually, this was just a little trio.
